text: The diagonal Ramsey number R(k) is the least n such that every two-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on n vertices contains a monochromatic clique on k vertices.
Erdős and Szekeres showed in 1935 that R(k) is at most the binomial coefficient 2k-2 choose k-1, which is roughly 4 to the power k.
Erdős used a random colouring in 1947 to prove the lower bound R(k) greater than 2 to the power k/2, an early landmark of the probabilistic method.
In 2023 Campos, Griffiths, Morris and Sahasrabudhe proved R(k) is at most (4 - epsilon)^k, the first exponential improvement of the classical upper bound.
The exact value R(5) remains unknown; it is only known to lie between 43 and 46, while R(4) equals 18.
Euclid proved that there are infinitely many primes by considering one plus the product of any finite list of primes.
The prime number theorem states that the number of primes up to x is asymptotic to x divided by the natural logarithm of x.
Dirichlet's theorem guarantees infinitely many primes in every arithmetic progression a, a+d, a+2d with gcd(a, d) = 1.
Zhang proved in 2013 that there are infinitely many pairs of primes differing by at most 70 million, later reduced to 246 by the Polymath project.
The polynomial n^2 + n + 41 found by Euler produces primes for n from 0 to 39 but gives 1681 = 41^2 at n = 40.
The Transformer architecture replaces recurrence entirely with self-attention, allowing all positions of a sequence to be processed in parallel.
Scaled dot-product attention divides the query-key dot products by the square root of the key dimension before applying a softmax.
Multi-head attention runs several attention functions in parallel on different learned projections and concatenates their outputs.
Because self-attention is permutation invariant, Transformers add positional encodings, originally sinusoids of different frequencies, to the input embeddings.
The cost of full self-attention grows quadratically with sequence length, which motivated sparse and linear attention variants.
Lean 4 is an interactive theorem prover and functional programming language based on dependent type theory.
Mathlib is the community library of formalised mathematics for Lean, covering algebra, analysis, topology and number theory.
In Lean a proof that still contains the sorry placeholder compiles with a warning, so the checker must reject any declaration that uses sorry.
The command #print axioms lists which axioms a theorem depends on, such as propositional extensionality, choice and quotient soundness.
The miniF2F benchmark contains olympiad-level competition problems stated formally, used to evaluate automated theorem provers.
A graph is planar if it can be drawn in the plane without edge crossings; Kuratowski characterised planar graphs by forbidden subdivisions of K5 and K3,3.
The four colour theorem, proved with computer assistance by Appel and Haken in 1976, says every planar map can be coloured with four colours.
Euler's formula for connected planar graphs states that vertices minus edges plus faces equals two.
A bipartite graph contains no odd cycle, and conversely every graph without odd cycles is bipartite.
Turán's theorem gives the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices that contains no complete subgraph on r+1 vertices.
The Gaussian integral of e to the minus x squared over the whole real line equals the square root of pi.
The gamma function extends the factorial, with Gamma(n+1) = n! for every non-negative integer n.
The integral from zero to infinity of x cubed times e to the minus x equals 3 factorial, that is 6, by the gamma function identity.
Integration by parts transfers a derivative from one factor of an integrand to the other at the cost of a boundary term.
The fundamental theorem of calculus links differentiation and integration: the derivative of the integral of f from a to x is f(x).
RSA encryption relies on the difficulty of factoring the product of two large primes.
Diffie and Hellman introduced public-key key exchange in 1976 based on the hardness of the discrete logarithm problem.
Shor's algorithm would factor integers in polynomial time on a large quantum computer, breaking RSA.
Lattice-based schemes such as Kyber are believed to resist quantum attacks and were standardised for post-quantum cryptography.
A cryptographic hash function should be preimage resistant and collision resistant; SHA-256 produces 256-bit digests.
The law of large numbers states that the sample mean of independent identically distributed variables converges to the expected value.
The central limit theorem says suitably normalised sums of independent variables with finite variance converge in distribution to a normal law.
The birthday paradox: in a group of 23 people the probability that two share a birthday exceeds one half.
Markov's inequality bounds the probability that a non-negative random variable exceeds a by its expectation divided by a.
A Markov chain is memoryless: the next state depends only on the current state, not on the earlier history.
The P versus NP problem asks whether every problem whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time.
Cook and Levin proved that Boolean satisfiability is NP-complete, the first problem shown to be so.
Karp showed in 1972 that 21 combinatorial problems, including clique and vertex cover, are NP-complete.
The travelling salesman decision problem is NP-complete, while its Euclidean version admits a polynomial-time approximation scheme.
Primality testing is in P, as shown by the deterministic AKS algorithm published in 2002.
A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is non-zero.
The spectral theorem says every real symmetric matrix can be diagonalised by an orthogonal matrix and has real eigenvalues.
The singular value decomposition factors any real matrix as an orthogonal matrix times a diagonal matrix times another orthogonal matrix.
The rank-nullity theorem: the dimension of the domain equals the rank plus the dimension of the kernel.
Gaussian elimination solves a system of n linear equations using on the order of n cubed arithmetic operations.
Fermat's little theorem: if p is prime and a is not divisible by p, then a to the power p-1 is congruent to 1 modulo p.
Andrew Wiles completed the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 1995 via the modularity of semistable elliptic curves.
The Chinese remainder theorem reconstructs an integer modulo a product of pairwise coprime moduli from its residues.
Every integer greater than one factors uniquely into primes, which is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic.
The product of two consecutive integers n(n+1) is always even, since one of the two factors is even.
Stochastic gradient descent updates parameters using the gradient of the loss on a small random mini-batch.
Adam combines momentum with per-parameter adaptive learning rates estimated from running averages of squared gradients.
Convex functions have no spurious local minima: every local minimum is a global minimum.
Dropout randomly zeroes activations during training to reduce co-adaptation and overfitting.
Batch normalisation standardises layer inputs using mini-batch statistics, which often speeds up training.
